code: model_fit_table <- function(models, n) {   rows <- lapply(names(models), function(label) {     object <- models[[label]]     data.frame(       model = label,       family = as.character(object$family[1L]),       parameters = object$df.fit,       logLik = -object$G.deviance / 2,       AIC = gamlss::GAIC(object, k = 2),       BIC = gamlss::GAIC(object, k = log(n)),       converged = isTRUE(object$converged),       row.names = NULL     )   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  coefficient_table <- function(object, parameters) {   rows <- lapply(parameters, function(parameter) {     estimate <- stats::coef(object, what = parameter)     data.frame(       parameter = parameter,       term = names(estimate),       estimate = unname(estimate),       row.names = NULL     )   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  fitted_summary <- function(values) {   rows <- lapply(names(values), function(quantity) {     x <- values[[quantity]]     data.frame(       quantity = quantity,       minimum = min(x),       first_quartile = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.25)),       median = stats::median(x),       mean = mean(x),       third_quartile = unname(stats::quantile(x, 0.75)),       maximum = max(x),       row.names = NULL     )   })   do.call(rbind, rows) }  response_profile <- function(x) {   c(     observations = length(x),     zero = sum(x == 0),     interior = sum(x > 0 & x < 1),     one = sum(x == 1)   ) }

title: Hyperbolic-secant-kernel Vasicek-type quantile distribution — HVASIQ
text: Let $$H(w)=\frac{2}{\pi}\arctan\{\exp(w)\},\qquad h(w)=\frac{1}{\pi\cosh(w)},$$ $$q(u)=H^{-1}(u)= \log\left\{\tan\left(\frac{\pi u}{2}\right)\right\}.$$ fixed \(\tau\(0,1)\), define $$=\sqrt{\frac{1-\sigma}{\sigma}},\qquad z=\{q(x)-q(\mu)\}+q(\tau).$$ cumulative distribution function density $$F(x\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)=H(z)$$ $$f(x\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)=\frac{h(z)}{h\{q(x)\}}.$$ quantile function $$Q(p\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)= H\left[q(\mu)+\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{1-\sigma}} \{q(p)-q(\tau)\}\right].$$ Consequently, \(Q(\tau)=\mu\); \(\mu\) exactly conditional \(\tau\)-th quantile conditional mean general. GAMLSS family uses analytical derivatives. one observation, let $$d=q(y)-q(\mu),\quad z=ad+q(\tau),\quad T=\tanh(z),\quad S=\operatorname{sech}^2(z),$$ $$b=\frac{1}{2\sigma(1-\sigma)},\qquad g=\frac{\pi}{\sin(\pi\mu)}.$$ \(\ell\) individual log-likelihood contribution, $$\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mu}=agT,$$ $$\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\sigma}=b(adT-1),$$ $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\mu^2} =g^2\{-\cos(\pi\mu)T-^2S\},$$ $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\mu\,\partial\sigma} =-abg(T+adS),$$ $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\sigma^2} =b^2\{2(1-2\sigma)-(3-4\sigma)adT-^2d^2S\}.$$ conditional mean variance elementary closed forms evaluated numerical integration quantile function. fixed level supplied quantile argument. stored family definition embedded numeric literal family components used GAMLSS; global variable required.

title: Logistic-kernel Vasicek-type distribution with quantile parameterization — LVASIQ
text: Let \(\mathrm{logit}(u)= \log\left(\frac{u}{1-u}\right)\) \(\Lambda(z)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}\), \(\lambda(z)= \Lambda(z)\left[1-\Lambda(z)\right]\). Define $$z = \sqrt{\frac{1-\sigma}{\sigma}} \left[\mathrm{logit}(x)-\mathrm{logit}(\mu)\right] +\mathrm{logit}(\tau).$$ Cumulative distribution function $$F(x\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)=\Lambda(z).$$ Probability density function $$f(x\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)= \sqrt{\frac{1-\sigma}{\sigma}} \frac{\lambda(z)}{x(1-x)}.$$ Quantile function $$Q(p\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau)= \Lambda\!\left\{ \mathrm{logit}(\mu) +\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{1-\sigma}} \left[\mathrm{logit}(p)-\mathrm{logit}(\tau)\right] \right\}.$$ construction \(Q(\tau)=\mu\), .e. \(\mu\) \(\tau\)-th quantile. Note , unlike normal-kernel Vasicek distribution, logistic kernel yield closed-form mean; particular \(E(X)\neq\mu\) general. GAMLSS family uses analytical derivatives. one observation, let $$=\sqrt{\frac{1-\sigma}{\sigma}},\qquad d=\mathrm{logit}(y)-\mathrm{logit}(\mu),\qquad P=\Lambda\left\{ad+\mathrm{logit}(\tau)\right\},$$ define $$V=P(1-P),\qquad b=\frac{1}{2\sigma(1-\sigma)},\qquad g=\frac{1}{\mu(1-\mu)}.$$ \(\ell\) denotes individual log-likelihood contribution, first derivatives $$\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\mu} =-ag(1-2P)$$ $$\frac{\partial\ell}{\partial\sigma} =-b\left\{1+ad(1-2P)\right\}.$$ second cross derivatives $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\mu^2} =g^2\left\{ (1-2\mu)(1-2P)-2a^2V \right\},$$ $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\mu\,\partial\sigma} =abg\left\{ (1-2P)-2adV \right\},$$ $$\frac{\partial^2\ell}{\partial\sigma^2} =b^2\left\{ 2(1-2\sigma) +ad(3-4\sigma)(1-2P) -2a^2d^2V \right\}.$$ expressions evaluated directly LVASIQ(); numerical differentiation used. mean variance components family object use numerical quadrature corresponding moments elementary closed forms.

text: Probability density function: $$f\left(x \mid \mu, \sigma, \tau\right) = \sqrt{\frac{1-\sigma}{\sigma}} \exp\left\{\frac{1}{2}\left[\Phi^{-1}(x)^2 - \left(\frac{\sqrt{1-\sigma}\left(\Phi^{-1}(x)-\Phi^{-1}(\mu)\right) - \sqrt{\sigma}\,\Phi^{-1}(\tau)}{\sqrt{\sigma}}\right)^2\right]\right\}.$$ Cumulative distribution function: $$F\left(x \mid \mu, \sigma, \tau\right) = \Phi\left(\frac{\sqrt{1-\sigma}\left(\Phi^{-1}(x)-\Phi^{-1}(\mu)\right) - \sqrt{\sigma}\,\Phi^{-1}(\tau)}{\sqrt{\sigma}}\right).$$ \(0<x<1\), \(0<\mu<1\), \(0<\sigma<1\), \(0<\tau<1\); \(\mu\) \(\tau\)-th quantile \(\sigma\) shape parameter.
